current_answer: NLnet CodeSupply and Restack remain open until 3 November 2026, 12:00 CET. Existing AI-generated code is not an automatic rejection: disclose significant use and let NLnet assess it. New proposals and funded deliverables still face policy v2.0 restrictions; the live form’s disclosure box is not permission to use GenAI for new writing.

catalogue_card.question: Used AI in your codebase—can you still seek an NLnet grant?
catalogue_card.text: Possibly. NLnet says old AI-generated code is evaluated, not automatically rejected; disclose significant use. New proposals and funded work face stricter rules. CodeSupply closes 3 November at 12:00 CET.

summary: The NLnet FAQ separates existing AI-generated code from AI-generated work proposed for funding; disclosure does not guarantee eligibility.
The FAQ describes a one-time exception for past AI-written text in pre-21-October proposals, but the announcement says before 20 October; ask NLnet about a 20 October filing.
CodeSupply remains open through 3 November 2026 at 12:00 CET, subject to project, location and open-licence rules.
uncertainty: Issuer FAQ and announcement differ on the one-time exception cutoff for AI-written proposals submitted on 20 October 2026.
NLnet evaluates existing code, future work and award case by case; no applicant decision was inspected.
First-party analytics and applicant outcomes are unavailable.
freshness_note: NLnet CodeSupply call, live form, policy v2.0 and dedicated FAQ checked 24 October 2026. Other catalogue rows retain their own dates.
